clue.text: Expert in copper and iodine backing polar region

indicators.note: backing means the assembled letters are read backwards, from the end
in places the expert's letters inside the copper's

parts.note: a copper is a police officer, a PC (police constable)
an ace is an expert
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A specialist in two chemical elements turns their attention to the Arctic.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests the chemical symbol Cu, but here it is the slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A polar ice cap is the frozen covering of land around a pole, so the term names that region.

clue.text: Result of appraisals quite out of place in serious situation — is not to be repeated

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the shortened crisis
the word 'is' appears twice in crisis, and saying it must not be repeated drops one copy

parts.note: a crisis is a serious situation
taken as written

indicators.note: letters out of place are put in a new arrangement

parts.note: anagram fodder as written

explanation.surface: A tense meeting where reviews have gone badly and someone insists a remark must not be repeated.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'is' appears twice in the serious situation, so 'is not to be repeated' tells you to remove just one copy.
explanation.definitionFit: Critiques are written assessments, the output of reviewing or evaluating something.

clue.text: Ballet heroine children adore? Not very

indicators.note: not very means the letter for very is removed from the word

parts.note: to adore is to love

explanation.surface: A ballerina wonders whether young audiences really worship her.
explanation.definitionFit: Chloe is the heroine of Ravel's ballet Daphnis and Chloe.

clue.text: Marker to put symbol on sheep — part of occult ritual?

parts.note: a pen is a marker for writing
to tag something is to attach a label or symbol to it
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A farmer marks a sheep with a sign, and a passer-by wonders if it is witchcraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The five-pointed star is a classic emblem drawn in magic ceremonies, hence the question mark for an example.

clue.text: Astronomical phenomena: question, when repeated, is about radius

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: is about means the repeated word goes around the radius letter

parts.note: repeated stands for the word for when a second time, so its letters come again
R is the abbreviation for radius in geometry

explanation.surface: An astronomer asks a question twice about the radius of a heavenly body.
explanation.definitionFit: Quasars are extremely bright, distant galactic nuclei, a type of object studied in astronomy.

clue.text: "Search interrupted by odd bits of rain?" one asks

indicators.note: interrupted by means the search word is broken open to take the other letters

parts.note: a quest is a search

indicators.note: odd bits are the first and third letters of the word rain

parts.note: first and third letters

explanation.surface: Someone wonders aloud whether a search party was stopped by scattered showers.
explanation.definitionFit: A querist is a person who puts questions, an inquirer.

clue.text: Irish saint's name attached to opera

indicators.note: attached to means the name letter is joined on after the opera

parts.note: Aida is Verdi's opera

explanation.surface: An Irish holy man's name is linked to an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Aidan of Lindisfarne was an Irish monk who evangelised Northumbria and is venerated as a saint.

clue.text: A limitation in Government? Commonplace

parts.note: a bound is a limit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A query about restrictions within government, dismissed as an everyday matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abounding is plentiful, found everywhere, so it is commonplace.

clue.text: Round of applause's volume in social gathering reduced

indicators.note: in places the volume letter inside the shortened gathering
reduced means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a salon is a gathering of guests in a fashionable home

explanation.surface: The noise of clapping at a party has been turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a burst, such as a sudden outburst of cheering or clapping.

clue.text: Crime involving random lone assault, say

indicators.note: involving means the crime word wraps around the other letters

parts.note: vice is wrongdoing, crime

indicators.note: random signals the letters are mixed up

parts.note: anagram fodder as written

explanation.surface: A report describes an offence committed in an unprovoked attack by a single person.
explanation.definitionFit: Assault is an example of violence, hence the 'say'.

clue.text: Simple example of art degree a great many left incomplete

indicators.note: left incomplete means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: oodles means lots, a great many

explanation.surface: A student's art qualification is left unfinished after many simple sketches.
explanation.definitionFit: A doodle is an idle, rough drawing, a very basic piece of artwork.

clue.text: Freedom in African country I discounted? Not I, after revolution

indicators.note: discounted means the letter is left out of the country

parts.note: Liberia is a country in West Africa
taken as written

indicators.note: after revolution means these letters have been turned about into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder as written

explanation.surface: A question of whether freedom has come to an African nation, with someone insisting they were not excluded after an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: Liberia contains two Is; either one may go, leaving the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberation is the act of setting free, so it stands for freedom gained.

clue.text: Twelve notes about rings

indicators.note: about means the notes go around the rings

parts.note: N is an abbreviation for note, so two notes are NN
O is shaped like a ring, so two rings are OO

explanation.surface: A dozen musical notes surround some bells being rung.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twelve' looks like a number to count notes, but it is the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Noon is twelve o'clock midday.

clue.text: Seeing lower reputation

parts.note: under means lower, beneath
standing is status or reputation

explanation.surface: Recognising that one's good name has fallen.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing in the sense 'I see' means grasping, comprehension of a point.

clue.text: Insiders upset about ordinary comments from mockers

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the ordinary letter
upset means the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder as written
O is an abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: People within an organisation are annoyed by mundane remarks from those who ridicule them.
explanation.definitionFit: Derision is scornful ridicule; its plural names the jeering remarks scoffers make.

clue.text: With swellings, no failure in accommodating most recent

indicators.note: accommodating means the failure word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a dud is a failure
late can mean most recent, a sense given in Chambers, as in 'the late news'

explanation.surface: Something has no failure in accommodating the latest developments.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodulated describes a surface bearing nodules, small lumps or growths.

clue.text: Kitchen appliance right to be included among diverse cargoes

indicators.note: to be included among means the right letters sit inside the other letters
diverse signals the letters are varied into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder as written
OK means all right, correct

explanation.surface: A household oven is correctly listed among various ship's freight.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas cooker is a stove fuelled by gas, a standard kitchen appliance.

clue.text: Something for breakfast? Clear off spread, say — good stuff initially following

parts.note: scram means clear off, go away
ink or dye that bleeds has spread
EG (for example) is what 'say' means

indicators.note: initially means take just the first letter

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: Someone is told to leave after spreading butter, with good things to come.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrambled eggs are a standard cooked breakfast dish, hence the question mark for an example.

clue.text: Mostly angry over Poles securing good gifts of the Church?

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the first piece above the second
mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: livid means very angry

indicators.note: securing means the poles hold the good letter between them

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Someone furious over Poles taking hold of presents from the Church.
explanation.walkthrough: A living is a church office with an income, in the gift of a patron, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Livings are benefices, posts as parish clergy that a patron grants to a priest.

clue.text: British shirking extra responsibility

indicators.note: shirking means the British letter evades its duty and is left out

parts.note: a bonus is an extra

explanation.surface: A British worker avoids an additional duty.
explanation.definitionFit: The onus is the burden or duty that falls on someone.

clue.text: Area of Israel Genesis upheld (English version)

indicators.note: upheld in a down clue means the letters are lifted so they read upwards

parts.note: Gen is the abbreviation for the book of Genesis

explanation.surface: A biblical region is supported in an English translation of Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: The Negev is the desert region covering southern Israel.

clue.text: Stripping, perhaps, is outrageous in elevator

indicators.note: is outrageous signals the letters behave wildly and are mixed up

parts.note: anagram fodder as written
anagram fodder as written

explanation.surface: Someone undressing in a lift is behaving scandalously.
explanation.definitionFit: Stripping bares the body, a kind of revealing or exposure; the 'perhaps' marks it as one example.

clue.text: Travelled by horse to old American ballet

parts.note: rode is the past tense of ride, to travel on horseback

explanation.surface: Someone rode on horseback to an old American dance show.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodeo is Aaron Copland's 1942 ballet, set in the American West.

clue.text: Tense humour surrounding special plot point

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: surrounding means the humour word goes around the special letter

parts.note: wit is humour

explanation.surface: A writer's nervous humour hovers around a particular moment in the story.
explanation.definitionFit: A twist is an unexpected development in a narrative, a turning point in the plot.

clue.text: Are Spain occupying first place? Not at present

parts.note: an are is a metric unit of area, 100 square metres, abbreviated A

indicators.note: occupying means Spain's letter sits inside first place

parts.note: gold is awarded for first place
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A query whether Spain is leading the table, answered that it is not right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are' looks like the verb but is the unit of area. The definition says something belongs to the distant past rather than now.
explanation.definitionFit: Age-old means ancient, existing since long ago rather than belonging to the current moment.

clue.text: Is very critical of return of metal tools?

indicators.note: return of means the metal word is read backwards

parts.note: tin is a metal
picks are digging tools

explanation.surface: A hardware buyer complains loudly about the return of metal implements.
explanation.definitionFit: To nitpick is to find fault over trivial details, being excessively fussy.

clue.text: Food etc not supporting plans

indicators.note: not means the supporting word is taken away

parts.note: provisions are supplies of food and drink
pro means in favour of, supporting

explanation.surface: Plans that leave out food and drink supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Visions are imagined schemes for the future, ambitions or plans.

clue.text: Foolish lover to finish little inspired by Romeo? On the contrary

parts.note: to do something in is to finish it, so do can mean finish

indicators.note: inspired by, reversed by 'on the contrary', means the little word takes in the Romeo letter
on the contrary flips the stated relation, so the little word holds Romeo rather than the other way round

parts.note: a tad is a little
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A doting suitor finishes a little piece inspired by Romeo, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally, TAD would go inside R, which is impossible; 'On the contrary' says R goes inside TAD instead, giving TARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A dotard is someone who dotes, a feeble-minded person foolishly fond, especially an old one.
